newsitem.title: IRAN: Zanganeh tipped as new Iranian oil minister.
newsitem.headline: Zanganeh tipped as new Iranian oil minister.

text.p: Energy Minister Bijan Namdar Zanganeh has been widely tipped in Iranian media to become Iran's new oil minister under President Mohammad Khatami who formally takes office on Monday.
The official Iranian news agency IRNA late on Sunday carried local reports detailing possible cabinet appointments under the new Khatami administration.

Zanganeh -- if he is nominated by Khatami and approved by the country's parliament -- would replace veteran Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh who is expected to retain an important position in a mediating council headed by outgoing president Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani.
As energy minister Zanganeh oversaw Iran's domestic power sector and its non-petroleum related energy sector.
Mohammad Khatami takes the presidential oath of office on Monday, sealing his landslide election victory in May.
The 54-year-old moderate Shi'ite cleric has not made known publicly his cabinet appointments or whether he will retain cabinet ministers that served under Rafsanjani.
Iran is the world's third largest oil exporter behind Saudi Arabia and Norway and is the second largest producer in the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC).
Daily crude output is 3.6 million barrels per day (bpd).
Speculation in local newspapers over the composition of Khatami's first cabinet has been rife in recent weeks.
